description: A doctoral research seminar on the foundations of modern cryptography: security definitions and reductions, pseudorandomness, zero-knowledge proofs, secure multi-party computation, lattice-based schemes, cryptanalysis and the move to post-quantum cryptography. Students read and critique recent papers, work through proofs and toy implementations in the maths lab, and prepare a research proposal with an artefact.
modelledOn: Katz and Lindell, Introduction to Modern Cryptography
Boneh and Shoup, A Graduate Course in Applied Cryptography
Peikert, A Decade of Lattice Cryptography
NIST post-quantum cryptography standardisation reports and draft standards
outcomes: State and compare security definitions for encryption, signatures and protocols, and write a reduction-based proof of a simple scheme.
Construct pseudorandom objects from one-way functions and explain the assumptions each construction needs.
Design and analyse commitments, sigma protocols and zero-knowledge proofs, including simulators, extractors and the removal of interaction.
Describe secure multi-party computation protocols for semi-honest and malicious adversaries and estimate their costs.
Explain how lattice problems yield encryption and signatures, and estimate concrete security with attack cost models.
Critique a published proof or attack, assess migration to post-quantum schemes, and defend a research proposal with an artefact.

units.title: Security definitions and reductions
topics: Computational security: negligible functions, probabilistic polynomial-time adversaries, asymptotic versus concrete security
Game-based definitions (IND-CPA, IND-CCA, EUF-CMA) and simulation-based definitions
Proofs by reduction and hybrid arguments; tightness and security loss
Idealised models: the random oracle, ideal cipher and generic group, and critiques of them
Critiquing a proof: common errors in published security arguments

units.title: One-way functions and pseudorandomness
topics: One-way functions, permutations and hard-core predicates
Pseudorandom generators from one-way functions and the length-extension argument
Pseudorandom functions from generators by a tree construction; Feistel networks and pseudorandom permutations
Message authentication and authenticated encryption; composition results
Number-theoretic assumptions (discrete log, CDH, DDH, RSA, factoring) and the five worlds of average-case complexity
Collision-resistant hashing: iterated and sponge constructions, and indifferentiability

units.title: Commitments and zero-knowledge proofs
topics: Commitment schemes: hiding and binding, discrete-log-based and hash-based commitments
Interactive proofs: completeness and soundness; sigma protocols for discrete logarithm knowledge
Zero knowledge: simulators, honest-verifier versus malicious verifier, proofs of knowledge and extractors
Removing interaction by hashing the challenge; security in the random oracle model and known pitfalls
Succinct arguments: arithmetisation, polynomial commitments, trusted setup versus transparent proofs
Applications: anonymous credentials, private payments and verifiable computation

units.title: Secure multi-party computation
topics: Adversary models: semi-honest and malicious; composition and the universal composability framework
Oblivious transfer and garbled circuits
Polynomial secret sharing and honest-majority protocols for arithmetic and Boolean circuits
Malicious security: cut-and-choose, authenticated sharing and zero-knowledge compilers
Threshold cryptography and links to homomorphic encryption
Applications and costs: private set intersection, auctions and joint statistics across hospitals

units.title: Lattice-based cryptography
topics: Lattices, shortest and closest vector problems, and the basis reduction algorithm LLL
LWE and SIS; worst-case to average-case reductions; ring and module variants
Public-key encryption and key encapsulation from LWE: correctness and noise analysis
Lattice signatures: hash-and-sign and Fiat-style signing with aborts
Fully homomorphic encryption: noise growth and bootstrapping
Concrete security: BKZ cost models, lattice estimators and parameter selection

units.title: Cryptanalysis case studies
topics: Generic attacks: birthday and meet-in-the-middle; differential and linear cryptanalysis
Implementation attacks: timing, cache, fault injection and padding oracles
Breaking deployed systems: weak randomness, nonce reuse in signatures and lattice small-root attacks on RSA
Break of a proposed post-quantum scheme: causes and lessons for scheme evaluation

units.title: Post-quantum transitions
topics: Quantum attacks: period finding against factoring and discrete log, quantum search against symmetric keys, and resource estimates
Standardisation of post-quantum schemes: lattice, hash-based, code-based and multivariate families and their status
Hybrid constructions, crypto-agility and the harvest-now-decrypt-later threat
Migration in African contexts: constrained devices, bandwidth limits and national identity and payment systems

units.title: Research seminar: proposal and artefact
topics: Surveying a topic and building a reading list
Formulating an open problem and a proof sketch
Building and testing a toy implementation or attack as an artefact
Presenting and defending the proposal

schedule.title: Computational security and game-based definitions
schedule.exercise: Write the IND-CPA game for a symmetric cipher, show that a deterministic cipher fails it with an explicit adversary, and compare asymptotic and concrete statements.

tasks.title: Plot adversary advantage against key length for a generic key-search attack and decide the key size for 2^-40 advantage at 2^80 work
Play the IND-CPA game against a deterministic cipher in the lab, build the winning adversary, and measure its advantage over 1000 rounds
Implement the EUF-CMA game against a textbook RSA signature and find a forgery that needs no signing query on the target message

schedule.title: Reductions, idealised models and proof critique
schedule.exercise: Prove security of a simple scheme by reduction with explicit loss, and identify the flaw in a supplied flawed proof.

tasks.title: Compute the security loss of a hybrid argument with q queries and derive the key length needed to keep 2^-40 advantage
Show that a hash function modelled as a random oracle gives a binding commitment, then explain what is lost when the oracle is instantiated
Step through a supplied reduction in the visualiser, mark the step where the simulator fails to program the oracle consistently, and repair it

schedule.title: One-way functions, generators and PRFs
schedule.exercise: Construct a pseudorandom generator from a one-way permutation with a hard-core bit, then build a pseudorandom function by the tree construction and test it statistically.

tasks.title: Compute modular exponentiation as a candidate one-way function for a 32-bit prime and measure the cost of inversion by brute force and baby-step giant-step
Stretch a short seed to 128 bits using a hard-core bit construction and run a frequency and runs test on 10000 outputs
Trace a four-round Feistel network in the visualiser for two plaintexts and show how round count affects distinguishability from a random permutation

schedule.title: Authentication, assumptions and hashing
schedule.exercise: Show that encrypt-and-MAC can leak information while encrypt-then-MAC does not, and map six number-theoretic assumptions by strength.

tasks.title: Build a distinguisher against encrypt-and-MAC for a deterministic MAC and measure its advantage over repeated messages
Draw the implications between DLog, CDH, DDH and RSA assumptions and mark which are known to be separated in generic groups
Implement an iterated hash with a toy compression function, mount a length-extension attack, then fix it with a sponge-style construction

schedule.title: Commitments, sigma protocols and zero knowledge
schedule.exercise: Prove that the sigma protocol for discrete log is complete, special-sound and honest-verifier zero-knowledge, and write its simulator and extractor.

tasks.title: Implement a commitment from a group of prime order, open it in two ways when the trapdoor is known, and show binding fails then
Step through the sigma protocol for knowledge of a discrete log in the visualiser, checking the verifier equation in each of ten runs
Write a simulator that produces accepting transcripts without the witness, and test that real and simulated transcripts are statistically close

schedule.title: Non-interactive proofs and succinct arguments
schedule.exercise: Convert the sigma protocol into a non-interactive proof by hashing the challenge, show how omitting the statement from the hash breaks soundness, and survey SNARK designs.

tasks.title: Build the non-interactive proof by hashing the challenge, then forge a proof when the statement is not included in the hash input
Turn a small arithmetic circuit into a rank-one constraint system and check a satisfying assignment by matrix multiplication
Choose a proof system for a private-payment application in a scenario with prover cost, proof size and setup trust trade-offs, scored on fit

schedule.title: Security models, oblivious transfer and garbling
schedule.exercise: Run a garbled circuit for an AND gate with oblivious transfer on paper and in the lab, and compare semi-honest and malicious security for the same protocol.

tasks.title: Show a semi-honest protocol leaking a private input to a malicious party, and give the adversary strategy that achieves it
Garble an AND gate with random wire labels, evaluate it on all four inputs, and check the evaluator learns only the output
Share two secrets by degree-1 polynomials over a prime field, multiply the shares, reduce the degree and reconstruct the product

schedule.title: Malicious security and applications of MPC
schedule.exercise: Estimate the communication cost of a three-hospital joint statistic with semi-honest and malicious protocols, and discuss whether a threshold design is better.

tasks.title: Step through a cut-and-choose garbled circuit protocol, mark where cheating is caught, and compute the detection probability for 10 copies
Implement threshold decryption among 5 parties with threshold 3 and test that any 2 parties learn nothing about the key
Compute the private set intersection of two patient ID lists with a hash-and-blind protocol and measure cost as list size grows

schedule.title: Lattices, LWE and SIS
schedule.exercise: Find a short vector in a two-dimensional lattice by reduction, build a small LWE instance, and analyse decryption correctness and noise growth.

tasks.title: Reduce a 2D lattice basis by hand-guided steps, plot both bases and compute the shortest vector length
Generate an LWE instance with dimension 8 and modulus 97, recover the secret by brute force and show how it scales with dimension
Implement LWE encryption of single bits, estimate the decryption failure rate over 10000 trials and tune parameters to push it below 1 percent

schedule.title: Lattice signatures, FHE and concrete security
schedule.exercise: Compare a lattice signature with a classical one on size and speed, analyse noise in homomorphic evaluation, and select parameters for 128-bit security.

tasks.title: Run signing with rejection sampling on toy parameters and plot the acceptance rate against the norm bound
Track noise growth through a chain of homomorphic additions and multiplications and find the depth at which decryption fails
Use a cost model to estimate the block size and bit security for five parameter sets and select the smallest set meeting 128 bits

schedule.title: Cryptanalysis case studies
schedule.exercise: Break a toy cipher with a differential attack, exploit a padding oracle, recover a key from nonce reuse, and write a short post-mortem on a broken post-quantum candidate.

tasks.title: Build a difference distribution table for a 4-bit S-box, find the best differential, and use it to recover one key nibble from chosen plaintexts
Mount a padding oracle attack against a toy decryption service and recover a 16 byte message with a count of oracle queries
Recover a signing key from two signatures that reused the same nonce in a toy discrete-log signature scheme

schedule.title: Post-quantum transition
schedule.exercise: Draft a migration plan for a national payment platform, sorting systems by data lifetime and device limits, with a hybrid mode and a rollback strategy.

tasks.title: Estimate the logical qubits and time for breaking 2048-bit RSA and 256-bit symmetric keys under stated assumptions, and compare the two threats
Compare key, signature and ciphertext sizes of five post-quantum candidates against RSA and elliptic-curve schemes and chart the bandwidth cost
Plan the post-quantum migration of a national identity card system in a scenario with old readers and low bandwidth, scored on risk reduction and cost

schedule.title: Research seminar: proposal and artefact
schedule.exercise: Present a research proposal with a survey, an open problem, a proof sketch and a small artefact, and answer questions from a seminar panel.

tasks.title: Draw a map of related work for your topic with the main assumptions and models of each paper, and mark the gap you target
Build a toy implementation of your chosen primitive or attack and run it on three parameter sizes to report cost and success
Defend your proposal before a panel in a scenario that questions the model, assumptions and artefact, scored on rigour and honesty about gaps
